summary: Working in philosophy and other fields, Lichtenberg studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1769. He subsequently held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1769 to 1799.

Curtius, a linguist, studied at Bonn under Ritschl, Lassen, and Schlegel, and at Berlin under Bopp. He held posts at Berlin, Vitzthum-Gymnasium Dresden, Prague, Kiel, and served as professor of classical philology at Leipzig from 1862 to 1885.
Forster worked in Indology and other fields after studying at Saint Peter's School. He held posts at Vilnius University (1784–1787) and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (circa 1788–1793).

Working in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology, Grotefend studied at Lessing-Gymnasium from circa 1792 to 1795 and at the University of Göttingen from circa 1795 to 1797.

Huth, a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1885 to 1889. He held a post at the University of Berlin from circa 1891 to 1906.

Kaibel worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Rostock (circa 1879–1882), University of Breslau (circa 1882–1883), University of Greifswald (circa 1883–1886), and University of Göttingen (circa 1897–1901).

Dissen was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1803 to 1807. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (circa 1812–1813) and Göttingen (circa 1813–1837).

Dursch studied theology, philosophy, and Indology at Tübingen, and Sanskrit under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy at Paris. Specializing in Indology and religious studies, he became a professor at Johann-Vanotti-Gymnasium Ehingen in 1829.

A scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Morgenstierne studied at Oslo, Bonn, and Berlin under Konow, Lüders, and Schulze. He was a professor at Gothenburg (1930) and Oslo (1937–1962).
Simmel worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Berlin from circa 1876 to 1881 and later held a post there from circa 1885 to 1914.

Freytag studied at Göttingen and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. Active in linguistics, he held positions at Göttingen, the University of Königsberg, and served as professor of oriental languages at the University of Bonn from 1819 to 1861.

Hegel studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium, Tübinger Stift, Tübingen under Schelling, and Jena. Working in philosophy, he held posts at the University of Jena (circa 1801–1807), University of Heidelberg (circa 1816–1818), and University of Berlin (circa 1818–1831).

Von Simson, a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, studied at Mainz and Göttingen. He worked as an editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1968–1977) and served as professor at the University of Oslo (1977–2003).

Von der Gabelentz studied at Jena, Leipzig, and TU Dresden. A scholar of sinology, linguistics, and japanology, he was professor at Leipzig (1878–1889) and professor of East Asian languages and general linguistics at Berlin from 1889.

Kennedy, a scholar of sinology and linguistics, studied at the University of Berlin under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke from circa 1932 to 1935. He subsequently held a post at Yale University from circa 1935 to 1960.

Keyworth studied at UC Santa Barbara and UCLA under Robert Buswell, Ronald Egan, Shuizhao Wang, and William F. Powell. Active in Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology, he held posts at Colorado (2001) and Saskatchewan (attested 2019).

Grierson studied at St Bees, Shrewsbury, and Trinity College Dublin. Active in linguistics and Indology, he served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1873–1903), the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and SOAS University of London (1917–1925).
Jacob worked in the field of Indology. He was a colonel in the Bombay Staff Corps (attested 1888) and the Indian Army (attested 1909), and was a fellow at the University of Mumbai (attested 1894).

Baumann, an Indology specialist, earned his PhD at the University of Heidelberg and studied at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen. He held posts at the University of Tübingen and Tübingen University Library from 1976 to 2001.

Cardona studied at NYU, Yale under Paul Thieme and Warren Cowgill, and in India. Specializing in Indology and linguistics, he was a fellow at CASBS (1971–1972) and professor of linguistics at the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1965–2005).
